mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative when GDP growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment signals economic strength, boosting consumer spending and equity markets in 5 days.
failure_condition: No positive returns when unemployment drops below 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rises and Fed Funds increase, tighter monetary policy may slow growth, negatively impacting S&P 500 in 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur despite the combined signal.

mechanism_narrative: Rising Fed Funds rates indicate tighter monetary policy, potentially reducing borrowing and slowing economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur when Fed Funds exceed 3%.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production suggests strong economic output, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns occur with rising industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts indicates weaker demand, potentially slowing economic growth and leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur when housing starts drop below 1200.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales and Fed Funds rise together, higher rates may dampen consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur despite the combined signal.

mechanism_narrative: Strong payroll growth indicates a robust labor market, boosting economic activity and leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: No positive returns when payroll exceeds 150,000.
